speaker: Doctor
text:
Please describe the appearance of your rash in detail, including any patterns like a "slapped cheek" or a lacy reticular pattern on your extremities.

Also, have you noticed any joint pain, swelling, or a "sandpaper" texture to the skin?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The classic presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the extremities, preceded by mild viral prodromal symptoms, is highly characteristic of Parvovirus B19 infection. No further tests are required at this time.
